summary: Corporate DPI rewriting TCP sequence numbers causing intermittent gRPC reconnects on private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported frequent short-lived gRPC connection drops between their hosted agents and our control plane. Drops began after a firewall rule rollout by the customer's security team.

Impact:
Control plane call failures caused roughly 5-10% of inference requests to return transient errors (Unavailable / 14) and triggered client reconnect storms; customer usage and latency SLOs were impacted for ~4 hours.

Environment:
Private deployment (VPC peering) to BrightLedger Analytics VPC. All traffic to Redwood control plane is over TLS (443) via peered route. Affected hosts: agent fleet in private subnets (10.60.*/24).

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer/support):
1) Start long-running streaming generation job from customer agent behind corporate perimeter appliance.
2) After 1-10 minutes, client reports: "rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing"; agent reconnects.
3) Frequently see immediate reconnect followed by successful resume.

Logs / Captures:
- Agent-side logs: repeated "transport: connection forced to close" and gRPC keepalive errors around connection loss time.
- Control plane logs: "stream closed with code Unavailable" with matching timestamps.
- Customer packet capture (pcap) from inside their perimeter appliance attached to ticket (pcap id: BL-20260310-01).

Observed pattern from pcap: sequence number gaps and unexpected TCP retransmit/dup-ACK bursts originating after the appliance. TLS payloads remain intact but TCP sequence numbers appear rewritten by appliance. There is no sign of packet loss on the NIC level prior to the appliance.

Additional context: customer applied a new corporate DPI/NGFW policy on 2026-03-10 which includes TLS inspection and some legacy TCP optimization features (labeled "TCP optimizer v2") that the vendor documents as doing "sequence normalization" for long-lived flows.
steps_to_reproduce: Run streaming gRPC request from agent behind vendor DPI appliance
Capture traffic on both sides of appliance to observe sequence rewrite
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
2026-03-10 09:12 - Customer reported spikes in gRPC disconnects.
2026-03-10 09:27 - Support requested pcap from customer; customer uploaded BL-20260310-01.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Network team inspected pcap; observed TCP sequence number jumps and immediate duplicate ACKs from server side following appliance. TLS records were not truncated; decryption not required to observe sequence anomalies.
2026-03-10 11:00 - Reproduced similar pattern in lab by placing Palo Alto/Checkpoint (vendor anonymized at customer's request) with "TCP optimizer" feature enabled between agent and control plane.

Hypothesis:
Corporate DPI is performing a sequence-number rewrite/normalization that is out-of-band with kernel TCP state on the agent and control plane, resulting in transient mis-synced window/seq expectations that trigger retransmits and gRPC transport closures. Because TLS is intact, application-layer messages are preserved but the transport resets cause gRPC to surface Unavailable.

Evidence collected:
- Packet-level diffs show seq delta introduced by appliance.
- When appliance is bypassed, connections remain stable for hours.
- Applying vendor-recommended disablement of "TCP optimizer/sequence normalization" in test removed failures.

Temporary mitigation tried:
- Customer created a security policy to bypass DPI for control-plane egress IPs; observed immediate reduction in reconnects.
- Support enabled more aggressive client-side keepalive backoff (reduce frequency of immediate reconnects to avoid thundering reestablish).

Cross refs:
- Slack: #support (thread: SUP-131210-dpi-rewrite)
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/dpi-network-issues

resolution:
Root cause: Customer's perimeter DPI/NGFW was performing TCP sequence-number normalization/rewrites for long-lived TLS flows which produced transient transport-level inconsistency between endpoints and caused gRPC transports to close.

Immediate resolution steps implemented:
- Customer applied bypass rules for Redwood control plane IPs on the appliance (temporary security exception) — stopped reconnects.
- Customer engaged their firewall vendor; vendor provided guidance to disable 'TCP optimizer/sequence normalization' for TLS flows. Vendor validated fix in staging.
- Redwood deployed a small server-side resilience patch to back off reconnect attempts and add jitter which reduced load during the incident (PR #789).

Longer-term recommendations provided to customer:
1) Maintain explicit bypass rules for control-plane/control-plane-proxy IP ranges or use VPC endpoint/private link to avoid inline DPI for control plane traffic.
2) Disable TCP-level ALGs/sequence normalization features on perimeter devices for TLS flows.
3) If inspection is required, perform TLS inspection that preserves original seq/ack mapping or terminate inspection at an egress proxy that cooperates with endpoints.
4) Redwood will add a KB article documenting symptoms of sequence-number rewriting appliances and a troubleshooting checklist.

Ticket closed after customer confirmed stability for 48 hours and vendor confirmed permanent policy change on 2026-03-12.

customer_communication_summary: We identified that the customer's perimeter appliance was rewriting TCP sequence numbers which caused transient gRPC transport closures. Customer disabled the optimizer feature and applied a bypass for Redwood control plane IPs; vendor validated the permanent change. We shipped a small resilience tweak to the runtime and provided a set of mitigations and long-term recommendations. Customer reported no further disconnects after 48h.
